title: Transformations, Symmetry & Congruence
domains: Rigid transformations in the coordinate plane
standards_support: Represent translations, reflections and rotations using coordinates and precise geometric notation.
Describe transformations as functions that map preimages to images and preserve appropriate geometric structure.
Use sequences of rigid motions to establish or analyze congruence.
Analyze symmetry through transformations that map a figure onto itself.
Use transformations to explain tessellations, frieze patterns and repeating geometric designs.
Construct and communicate mathematical arguments using diagrams, coordinates, definitions and verified evidence.
mathematical_practices: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
Construct viable arguments and critique reasoning.
Look for and make use of structure.

u02-l01: Apply translation vectors to points and figures.
Recover or verify translation rules from coordinate evidence.
u02-l02: Reflect figures across coordinate axes and specified lines.
Connect reflection rules to geometric distance from the mirror line.
u02-l03: Rotate points and figures about the origin and other centers.
Use angle, direction and center information precisely.
u02-l04: Apply transformations in the stated order.
Distinguish composition order and explain noncommutativity through examples.
Describe a composite mapping from preimage to final image.
u02-l05: Use rigid motions to define and establish congruence.
Identify invariant distances and angle measures.
Connect transformation evidence to corresponding parts.
u02-l06: Identify and justify line, rotational and point symmetry.
Determine rotational order and angle where appropriate.
Distinguish visual appearance from a transformation that actually maps a figure onto itself.
u02-l07: Analyze tessellations and frieze patterns using transformations.
Design or critique a pattern for gaps, overlaps, symmetry and repeatability.

unit_evidence: Seven hardened printable lessons with written mathematical reasoning.
Foundation, Core and Extended practice pathways.
A 12-question mastery check drawn from a unit-aligned assessment bank.
Written corrections or targeted remediation when mastery evidence is incomplete.
Arcade Symmetry Studio & Transformation Design applied investigation with portfolio evidence.

assessment_expectations.automatic: Objective mastery-check responses may be scored by the local assessment engine.
assessment_expectations.human_review: Open explanations, constructions, design evidence, corrections and project rubric judgments require teacher, mentor or qualified reviewer judgment.
assessment_expectations.mastery: Target is 80% on objective evidence or documented correction/remediation evidence demonstrating the missed skills.
assessment_expectations.policy_note: Automated score evidence and human-reviewed portfolio evidence are complementary; neither should be represented as evidence the learner did not actually produce.
